match.reason: No bank point teaches the idea that style and form are shaped by purpose and in turn shape the reader's response in the Stage 5 Style chapter; the closest, Evaluating literary style, is Year 9 evaluation and is framed around judging a style rather than the two-way link between purpose and effect that the brief describes.

draft.title: Style and purpose
card: Style is the way a text is written: its word choice, sentence patterns, imagery and form. Every writer makes these choices to suit a purpose.
A text meant to persuade may use strong, emotive words, short punchy sentences and direct questions. A text meant to inform may use plain, exact words and calm, clear sentences.
A text meant to entertain or move a reader may use vivid imagery, varied sentence lengths and a form such as a poem or story.
Style also shapes how a reader responds. Short, sharp sentences can create urgency, while long, flowing ones can create a calm or dreamy mood.
draft.remember: Writers choose style to suit purpose, and the style guides the reader's response.

a.q: Why does a writer choose strong, emotive words and short punchy sentences for a speech urging people to save a local park?
opts: The style suits the purpose of persuading listeners
The style suits the purpose of informing with plain facts
The style suits the purpose of describing a calm scene
The style suits the purpose of recording events in order
a.why: Emotive words and short sentences push listeners to feel and act, which suits persuading. Plain facts are the style of informing, which does not rely on strong feeling.
a.clue: What does the speech want listeners to do?

b.q: Nina writes a fire safety leaflet for Year 7 students. It uses short sentences, simple words and numbered steps. What is the main effect of this style on readers?
opts: It makes the instructions clear and easy to follow quickly
It makes readers feel a dreamy, reflective mood
It makes readers angry about unsafe behaviour
It makes the leaflet sound like a personal diary
b.why: The leaflet's purpose is to inform and instruct, so plain words and numbered steps make it easy to follow. A dreamy mood suits long, flowing sentences and imagery, not a safety leaflet.
b.clue: Think about what the leaflet needs readers to do in a hurry.

a.best: The style suits the purpose of persuading listeners

b.best: It makes the instructions clear and easy to follow quickly
